_format: trine-eval Planner sprint entries (number, title, features, estimated_complexity, dependencies) extended with id, phase, repo, exit_criteria and level5_decisions. Each entry is meant to be pasted into the target repo's .harness/sprints.json as a new phase (a Level 5 edit of a sacred file), or to seed /trine-eval:harness-kickoff where the repo has no harness yet.

sprints.title: Session diagnostics hook: one event per settled process lifetime into .council/diagnostics.jsonl
features: Stage 1, SessionEnd only (ADR-0006 A1): the SessionEnd hook appends one kind=session event (schema 1.1) per non-empty settled process lifetime, derived by one pure function that a backfill command also calls; a /clear predecessor is settled at its successor's SessionEnd in the same process

the event per ADR-0006 A1 D1: usage, usage_by_model and sidechain_usage over the lifetime's own requests in the main transcript and the subagent files (each requestId once, fork copies left out); cost_usd = the closing cost-state minus the restored base (a fork's base from cost lineage); cost_state_usage_by_model; counts; the anchors; a UUIDv5 event_id; ts from the entries; a coverage block; sprint and phase from .harness/sprint-state.json at the end
compactions counted from compact_boundary entries, subagents as the larger of agent files and Agent/Task launches; no PreCompact or SubagentStart marker hooks
crew guard: with AUTOMATE_RUN set, council hooks write nothing (auto-mate commits a crew's leftovers with git add -A and counts them as changes)

Stage 2, after Stage 1: a SessionStart hook for the /clear hand-off, the fork base and recovery (re-appending a lifetime whose line is missing under the same event_id; recording an interrupted lifetime with exact tokens and cost_usd null)
hooks/enforce-append-only.sh covers .council/diagnostics.jsonl; rotate-audit-log.py handles it the same way; a producer skips an event_id already in the ledger or its newest rotated archive
scripts/measure-projection-cost.py appends a kind=projection-cost event when a .council/ exists
schema copy under schemas/diagnostic-event.schema.json kept byte-identical to cloud-catcher's (a test diffs them)

tests/schemas/diagnostic-event rewritten for schema 1.1: valid session events for settled, interrupted, fork and /clear lifetimes; each invalid session fixture rebuilt as an otherwise valid 1.1 event, so it fails only on its named keyword

henka-council's CLAUDE.md, README, instructions/controlled-artifacts.md and skills/council-kickoff/SKILL.md say one event per settled process lifetime, written by the hooks and the backfill command (ADR-0006 A1)
PowerShell parity or recorded deferral; tests with recorded fixture transcripts whose lifetimes and totals are known
exit_criteria: the recorded fixtures listed in ADR-0006 A1's Verification yield one session event per non-empty lifetime, with cost_usd and tokens as stated there for the stage shipped

a redacted fixture of the real cloud session yields five events of 7.1773923, 27.49865245, 0.9899525, 152.047308 and 62.2513088 USD, summing to 249.96461405; the fifth has ts 2026-11-04T22:20:42.265Z, its last subagent entry
a second firing on the same state appends nothing; with AUTOMATE_RUN set, nothing under .council/ changes
no prompt or response text appears in any event

status.note: PR #28 writes one cumulative event per exit; ADR-0006 A1 (D1 to D4 decided by the human 2026-11-06) replaces that with one event per settled process lifetime. The rework ships as a follow-up PR to henka-council #28: Stage 1 SessionEnd-only settled lifetime deltas, then Stage 2 the SessionStart hook

sprints.title: Rubrics and contract guidance for research reports and quantitative models

skills/eval-rubric/rubrics/quant-model.md: dimensions for correctness against closed-form or reference cases, reproducibility (seed determinism, pinned inputs), statistical validity (convergence, confidence intervals, calibration or backtest where applicable), code quality; hard thresholds: no reference-case parity test, or non-deterministic results under a fixed seed
rubrics/README.md decision guide rows and eval-rubric SKILL.md listing
sprint-contract/SKILL.md: a 'document deliverable' subsection: behavioral criteria for documents (commands that check sources, figures regenerated from code, word or section budgets), bucket guidance

exit_criteria: both rubrics load through eval-rubric

_status_convention: status.state is one of planned, in-progress, in-review, done, dropped; status.ref points at the PR or commit range; status.note records deviations from the sprint's features.
